items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: we got to be very good friends.

ctx.x: Gee I never heard that name.

Yeah. He was a bass player who played with Duke Ellington, he played in the Mills Blue Rhythm Band, he was the straw boss there in fact, and he had played with Benny Carter and with many, many. And he came originally from Chicago. He was a drummer in the Chicago Defender Band at one time. And so I met him and I knew about him. And he lived — at the time that I really got to know him was when I took the orthodontic course at Columbia University. Because then I lived with my wife at 175th Street in Washington…

different. And Bacon said, “That’s me there.” So and I remember I played the record for a whole week and tried to figure out who can that trumpeter be. And finally I hit, I said I think it might be Louis Metcalf. Well luckily I was into this early enough, Louis Metcalf was still alive and around, and I sort of knew him. And I asked him to come to the house, and I played him “In the House Blues.” And he said, “Yes, I have to admit, that’s me.” But, in other words he didn’t think much of it, although it’s great…
